meta.title: The Wind and the Sun
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Tom

paragraphs: On Wednesday, January thirteenth, it was half past seven, and the morning was cool. Tom walked to school with Lily and Pat. A few leaves lay on the path, and the low sun shone through the trees. Pat followed Tom and Lily with a big blue jacket over his arm. "Put on your jacket, Pat," said Lily. "Why should I wear it?" asked Pat. "I am not cold, and it is too big." "I know a story about that," said Tom. "Listen, and you will see the reason."

This was Tom's story. One day, the Wind and the Sun saw a traveler on a road. The man was dressed in a long brown coat. "Who can make that man take off his coat?" asked the Sun. "Possibly I can," said the Wind. "It is easy for me." The Wind blew hard, and the leaves flew around the man. But the man held his coat closed with both hands. The Wind blew harder, but it could not pull the coat away. "This is strange," said the Wind. "I do not believe it."

Then it was the turn of the Sun. The golden Sun came out from behind a cloud. It shone warm and bright on the road. Suddenly the man felt hot. He stopped and looked up at the sky. He took off his coat easily and carried it on his arm. The surprised Wind looked at the Sun. "How did you do that?" he asked. "I was kind, and you were hard," said the Sun.

That was the end of Tom's story. Pat stood still on the path. "The Sun was kinder," he said. "What happened to the Wind?" "He went home," said Tom. "If you push someone, he will hold on." "If you are kind, he will listen." Pat put on the jacket. "It is still too big, but I will wear it," he said.

At the school gate, the sun came out from behind a cloud. Pat felt warm in the jacket. Lily laughed. "Now you are just like the traveler," she said. Pat took off the jacket and carried it on his arm. "The Sun won again," said Tom. Then the three of them walked through the gate together.
text.summary: On a cool morning, Pat will not wear his jacket. Tom tells him the old tale of the Wind and the Sun, and Pat learns that kind help works better than force.
